Quiet parts louder, loud parts quieter
Standard mode only (All apps is always silent)
In the Sonos app, UPnP must be on under Account > Privacy & Security > Connection Security (default).
Lossless (PCM). Audio reaches the Sonos a little later: ideal for music, not lip-synced for video.

All apps: turn on \"Wireless debugging\" in Developer options once and pair. No root needed. After that the app turns it back on by itself, even after a reboot. Developer options must stay on; if Android asks about the Wi-Fi network, tick \"Always allow on this network\".
Sunus is open source under the MIT License and uses the components listed under \"Notices\".

1. Tap \"Start pairing\". \"Wireless debugging\" opens.\n2. Turn it on and tap \"Pair device with pairing code\".\n3. Leave the dialog open, pull down the notification shade and enter the 6-digit code in \"Pair Sunus\".
The app finds the port itself. If Developer options are still hidden: Settings > About phone > tap \"Build number\" 7 times.

The code does not go into this app. You enter it in the \"Pair Sunus\" notification. No input field? Expand the notification with its arrow. No notification? Allow notifications for Sunus and tap \"Start pairing\" again.
Please allow notifications, that\'s where the code is entered.
Unlock Developer options first: tap \"Build number\" 7 times, then come back and tap \"Start pairing\" again.
Open the pairing dialog, then enter the code here
Pairing dialog found. Now enter the 6-digit code.
Pairing dialog found. Enter the code in the notification.
The code has 6 digits. Please enter it again.
No pairing dialog found. Keep it open and enter the code and the port shown there, for example: 123456 37123
No pairing dialog found. Enter the code and the port from the dialog in the notification.
Paired, but the phone refused the connection. Please start pairing again.
Pairing failed. Check the code; the dialog must be open.
Paired. All apps is set up.
Wireless debugging not found. Is it on and is Wi-Fi connected?

No Wi-Fi address. Is the phone on Wi-Fi?
The Sonos does not accept the stream.
The Sonos can\'t reach the stream on the phone. Are both on the same network (no guest Wi-Fi, no VPN)?
The phone can\'t reach the speaker.
Turn on Wireless debugging in Developer options, stay on Wi-Fi and try again. Standard mode works without it.
Stop, wait a few seconds and start again. If it happens again, please share the report.
This can happen when Wireless debugging goes off or the Wi-Fi changes. Start again.
Check that Sunus may use the microphone, then start again.
Android may end the capture, for example when the screen locks. Start again, or set up All apps.
Confirm Android\'s capture prompt when starting. Once All apps is set up, the prompt no longer appears.
Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi as the speaker.
Close the app completely and open it again.
Check in the Sonos app that UPnP is on, then try again. If you have another speaker, try that one too.
Turn off any VPN and check the phone\'s local network permission for Sunus.
Check that the speaker is on and in the same Wi-Fi, then search for speakers again.
Please share the report so the crash can be fixed.
